correctness.rationale: All simple games through five players are generated independently both as minimal-winning antichains and as monotone Boolean truth tables. The two universes agree exactly. Properness, weak-order comparison, all relabeling orbits, and nine weighted representations are exact; Shapley-Shubik is independently replayed by pivotal-coalition and permutation formulas. The packaged verifier returns VERIFY_OK.

evidence: Aziz 2008 gives the simple-game, Shapley-Shubik, and Deegan-Packel definitions and studies computational access to the indices.
Freixas-Marciniak 2011/2013 shows Shapley-Shubik satisfies an egalitarian property while Deegan-Packel has counterexamples, demonstrating genuine structural differences.

Khmelnitskaya-Chessa 2020 proves \(DP_i(v)\) is the Shapley value of an auxiliary game built from the minimal winning coalitions, explaining affinity without forcing ordinal equivalence on the original game.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These broader theorems establish why comparison of the two indices is meaningful but do not determine the smallest proper game with a rank reversal or enumerate the first divergent stratum.

originality.rationale: Prior work defines and compares the Deegan-Packel and Shapley-Shubik models and proves a close Shapley-value relation, but the inspected sources do not give the sharp proper-game ranking boundary or its complete five-player census. The accepted statement is not implied by known computational complexity, monotonicity, egalitarian-property, or auxiliary-game identities.
residual_risks: An unindexed older enumeration, thesis, classroom note, or software output may contain the same five-player proper-game classification.

value.rationale: Shapley-Shubik and Deegan-Packel encode two classical and substantively different models of voting power. Properness is a standard institutional consistency condition. The smallest proper voting body where the two models strictly reverse a pairwise ranking is therefore a natural structural invariant. The complete first divergent stratum and the fact that all nine classes are weighted make the result directly reusable for weighted voting examples and index-comparison benchmarks.
